correctness.rationale: For \(s=\theta/2\), the coordinate identity is exact. Fixed-angle weighted Cauchy gives \(M_s(y)=\max\{1,c^2+h^2/y\}\); symmetric endpoints and real-phase equality vectors give \(m_s(y)=\min\{1/(1+y),h^2/y\}\). Piecewise monotonicity identifies the unique diagonal optimum and squared distortion \(2\). Averaging an arbitrary Hermitian quadratic form under \(v\mapsto-v\) cannot increase its best distortion, and lower/upper contact pairs force its real and imaginary cross coefficients to vanish at equality. Explicit endpoint and interior vectors verify sharpness; numerical sampling is supplementary only.

Determining the actual optimally conditioned Hermitian matrix is a natural finer geometric invariant, not determined by that scalar or by existential uniqueness. The computed unique form changes with \(\theta\) until a sharp semicircle threshold and then freezes exactly while the underlying Banach norms remain distinct. This is a complete natural-parameter metric classification, rather than an arbitrary finite sample or known-table recomputation.
